1902:
** ἐπεν-δύνω** [ῡ]
or **ἐπεν-δύω**, **put on over,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|ἐπὶ τοῦτον ἄλλον κιθῶνα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.195}}:—_middle_, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|-σάμενος χιτῶνα 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 3.7.4; πολλὰ σώματα Aeneas Gazaeus Rhetor [{5-6th c.AD}] “Theophrastus” p.60 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus:}}] —_passive_ (with _aorist 2_ _participle_ {{Refs 1st c.AD+|-δύντες 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 5.1.12)}}, **have on over,** [{{Refs 1st c.AD+|ἐσθῆτας ἐπενδεδυμένοι γυναικείας τοῖς θώραξι Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus [{1-2nd c.AD}] “Pelopidas” 11}}].
1903:
** ἐπεν-δύτης** [ῠ], ου, ὁ,
**robe** or **garment worn over** another, Ps.-Thes{{LXX+5th c.BC+|p.1, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “fragment” 439, LXX.1Ki.18.4; ἐ. χιτών 4th c.BC: Nicochares Comicus 5, compare 2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus Dion. “fragment” 325, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.45.}}
1913:
** ἐπιβιβ-άζω**
(_future_ {{LXX|-βιβῶ Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Hos.10.11, LXX.Hab.3.15), causal of ἐπιβαίνω}}, **put** one **upon**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγας ναῦς τοὺς ὁπλίτας 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.31}}; τινὰ ἐπὶ {{NT|τὸ ἴδιον κτῆνος NT.Luke.10.34}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Apollodorus Damascenus Mechanicus 3.1.1.}}
1917:
** ἐπιβουλ-ή**, ἡ,
**plan formed against** another, **plot, scheme**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.12, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.77, 86, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 4.148, etc.; ἐπιβουλὴν ἐπιβουλεύειν 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 13.18}}; πρός τινα against one, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 1.1.8; ἐξ ἐπιβουλῆς}} by **treachery, treacherously**, ἐξ ἐ. ἀποθανεῖν, ἐξ ἐ. φονεὺς εἶναι, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 2.1.5, 1.3, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 8.92, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 6.4.7, etc.; μετὰ ἐπιβουλῆς}} **designedly**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Lg.” 867a, +others}}
1925:
** ἐπιδείκ-νῡμι -νύω**, ἐπιδεικνύω
{{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“PPetr.” 2p.110 (3rd c.BC))}}, _future_ -δείξω: _aorist_ ἐπέδειξα, _Ionic dialect_ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|ἐπέδεξα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.42}}:—**exhibit as a specimen**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ach..” 765}}: generally, **display, exhibit**, [{{Refs 5th c.BC+|βίαν 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 11.14; τεκμήρια Aeschylus Tragicus [{4-5th c.BC}] “Supplices” 53 (Lyric poetry), etc.; ἑωυτόν τινι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.42; πᾶσαν τὴν Ἑλλάδα τινί [prev\. author] 3.135, compare 6.61; ἐ. τὸ στράτευμά τινι}}] **parade** it before.., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 1.2.14, compare “Cyr.” 5.5.5}}; of speeches, compositions, etc., ἐπιδειξάτω τῇ βουλῇ he **shall exhibit** his draft, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|“IG” 12.76.60; ἐ. λόγον Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Equites” 349; ῥαψῳδίαν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Leges” 658b, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 2.7 (_passive_); σοφίαν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Euthydemus” 274a, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Smp.” 3.3.}}]
**2**. more frequently in _middle_, **show off** or **display for oneself** or **what is one's own**, μουσικὰν ὀρθὰν ἐ. **give a specimen of his** _article_., {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “fragment” 32; ἐμὲ ἐπεδέξατο γυμνήν}} **exhibited** me naked, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.11; πάντα τὸν στρατόν}} **showed** all **his** army, {{Refs|[prev\. author] 7.146; ἐ. τὸν Ἀλέξανδρον}} **recall** Alexander, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Pyrrh.” 8; especially of one's personal qualities, ἐπιδείκνυσθαι τὴν αὑτοῦ δύναμιν Andocides Orator [{5-6th c.BC}] 4.14}}]; σοφίαν, πονηρίαν, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phdr.” 258a, 5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 20.4, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “An.” 1.9.16; ἐπιδείξασθαι αὑτὸν ἀβέβηλον “Inscription Prien.” 113.66 (1st c.BC).}}
**2.b**. ἐπίδειξαι.. ἅττ᾽ ἐδίδασκες **give a specimen of.. **, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nu.” 935; τὰ γυμνικά “POxy.” 42.5 (4th c.AD): _absolutely_}}, **show off, make a display of one's powers**, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|ἐπεδείκνυτο τοῖς λωποδύταις Aristophanes Comicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Ranae” 771}}]; ὃν.. ἐθεάσασθε ἐπιδεικνύμενον **giving a display** (of fighting in armour), {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “La.” 179e}}; of a rhetorician lecturing, {{Refs|[prev\. author] “Phdr.” 235a; πολλὰ καὶ καλά [prev\. author] “Grg.” 447a}}; of epideictic orators, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Rh.” 1391b26}}; of a musician, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus “VH” 9.36}}: with _participle_, ἐ. [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|ὑπερθέων Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Leges” 648d}}].
**II**. **show, point out**, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|τινὶ τὴν αἰτίαν [prev\. author] “Phd.” 100b, compare 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 1.177; τὴν πονηρίαν Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Protagoras” 346a}}]; ἐ. αὐτήν, ἥτις {{Refs|ἐστίν Pl.Comedy texts 173.5}}; ἐ. τὸν ἀλεκτρυόν᾽ ὡς ἐτυράννει **show, prove** that.., [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Av.” 483, compare 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 1.4; ὅτι.. Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Respublica” 391e}}], etc.: with _participle_, ἐ. πάντα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|ἐόντα μεγάλα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.30}}; ἐ. τινὰ φονέα ὄντα **show** that one is a murderer, variant in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 1.3, compare 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.64 (where perhaps ἐπ- ` _as an afterthought_ '); ἐ. τινὰ δωροδοκήσαντα}} **prove** that one took bribes, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Eq.” 832 (_anapaest meter_); ἐπιδείξω σε ταῦτα ὁμολογοῦντα Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Euthydemus” 295a, compare “Chrm.” 158d; ψυχὴν ἐ. πρες βυτέραν οὖσαν τοῦ σώματος [prev\. author] “Lg.” 892c}}]; ἐ. αὑτὸν φοβερὸν (i.e. [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|ὄντἀ καὶ μέγα δυνάμενον Andocides Orator [{5-6th c.BC}] 4.11}}]: with _accusative_, ἐ. ὅ τι ἂν ἐγκαλῇ {{Refs 4th c.BC+|ἐναντίον ἀνδρῶν τριῶν “PEleph.” 1.7 (4th c.BC), etc.:}} —_passive_, ἐπιδείκνυται αὐθέντης (i.e. ὤν) [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.4.9; ἐπεδείχθησαν οὐδὲν βελτίους ὄντες Isocrates Orator [{5-6th c.BC}] 4.145, compare 18.56; κινδυνεύσεις ἐπιδεῖξαι χρηστὸς εἶναι Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Memorabilia” 2.3.17}}] (ἐπιδεῖξαι secl. Cobet).
**II.2**. _middle_, [{{Refs 6th c.BC+|τῆς αἰτίας τὸ εἶδος Plato Philosophus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Phaedo” 100b; ἔργῳ ἐπεδείκνυτο, ὅτι.. Xenophon Historicus [{5-6th c.BC}] “Anabasis” 1.9.10, compare 4th c.BC: Isaeus Orator 5.30.}}]
1928:
** ἐπιδια-τάσσομαι**,
**make additions to a will,** NT.Gal.3.15.
1930:
** ἐπιδιορθ-όω**,
**correct afterwards**, {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|“GDI” 5039.9 (Hierapytna, 2nd c.BC):}} —_middle_, ἐ. τὰ λείποντα **to have** deficiencies **set right also, complete** unfinished **reforms,** NT.Tit.1.5; simply, **correct**, {{Refs 5th c.AD+|5th c.AD: Syrianus Philosophus et Rhetor “in Metaphorical” 167.11.}}
1931:
** ἐπιδύω **
(**ἐπιδρομ-δύνω** [ῡ] {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD(?): Manetho Astrologus 6.642)}}, _aorist 2_ ἐπέδυν, **set upon** or **so as to** **interrupt** an action, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|μὴ πρὶν ἐπ᾽ ἠέλιον δῦναι 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.413}}; ὁ ἥλιος μὴ ἐ. ἐπὶ {{LXX+1st c.AD+|τῷ παροργισμῷ ὑμῶν “Epistle to the Ephesians” 4.26, cf. LXX.Deu.24.15, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.324.}}
1937:
** ἐπιθῡμ-έω**,
**set one's heart upon** a thing, **long for, covet, desire**, with _genitive_ _of things_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.66, A. “Ag.” 216, etc.: also with _genitive_ _person_, Lys. 3.5, X. “An.” 4.1.14 (later with _accusative_ _person_, [Men.] cited in Clem.Al. “Strom.” 5.119, “Tab.Defix.” “Aud.” 271.45 (Hadrumetum, 3rd c.AD))}}; of political attachments, τῶν ἡμετέρων πολεμίων 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 4.28; ὀλιγαρχίας 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 20.3: with _infinitive_, **desire to** do, πλῶσαι 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.24; ἀπικνέεσθαι{{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. work] 116; περισσὰ δρᾶν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Trachiniae” 617, etc.}}: _absolutely_, **desire, covet**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Th. 6.92; ὁ ἀεὶ-ῶν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 313d, etc.}}; τὸ ἐπιθυμοῦν τοῦ πλοῦ, ={ἐπιθυμία}, **eagerness for** it, {{Refs|Th. 6.24}}:—_passive_, **to be desired**, τὰ ἐπιθυμούμενα 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Philebus” 35d.
1944:
** ἐπικατ-άρᾱτος** [ᾰρ], ον,
**accursed**, {{LXX+NT|LXX.Gen.3.14, NT.Gal.3.10, 13, “IG” 12(9).955 (from Euboea); ταῖς ἀραῖς “BMus.Inscription” 918.6 (Halic.).}}
1946: **Epicurean **, [_variant_ datesAnthology Palantina; οἱ Ἐπ. **the Epicureans **, {{Refs 2nd c.AD|Lucian}} (Middle Liddel)
1950:
Included with: ** ἐπιλήθ-ω**,
**cause to forget**, ὁ γάρ τ᾽ [ὕπνος] ἐπέλησεν ἁπάντων **laps one in forgetfulness** of all, {{Refs|Od. 20.85}}; ἡδονὴ σφέας ἐπιλήθουσα τῶν πάρος 2nd c.AD: Aretaeus Medicus “χρονίων νούσων θεραπευτικόν” 2.12; ἐπιλήσει σε ἀφροδισίων 2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Epistulae” 68:—_passive_, **to be forgotten**, in _perfect_ _participle_ ἐπιλελησμένος Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum LXX.Isa.23.16 {{NT|“NT.Luke.12.6”}}: _future_ **-λησθήσομαι** Vetus Testamentum Graece redditum “Wisdom of Solomon” 2.4.
**II**. _middle_, **ἐπιλανθάνομαι**, or more commonly **ἐπιλήθομαι**, _Aeolic dialect_ and _Doric dialect_ **-λᾱθ-** {{Refs|Alc. “Supp.” 25.6, S. “El.” 146 (Lyric poetry)}}_future_ -λήσομαι: _aorist 2_ **-ελᾰθόμην** 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Apologia” 17a: late _aorist 1_ **-ελήσατο** Nonnus Epicus 4th-5th c.AD(?) “Dionysiaca” 48.969: with _perfect_ _active_ λέληθα 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.46 {{Refs|Pi. “O.”(see.below)}}, but more frequently _passive_ **-λέλησμαι** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 188, Ar. “Nu.” 631, Lys. 26.1, Pl. “Phd.” 75d, +others}}: pi_perfect_ **-ελελήσμην** {{Refs|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 605, Pl. “Phd.” 73e, +others}}:—**let** a thing **escape** one, **forget, lose thought** **of**, c._genitive_, ὅπως Ἰθάκης ἐπιλήσεται (_Epic dialect_ _aorist_ _subjunctive_) {{Refs|Od. 1.57}}; οὐδ᾽ ὁ γέρων δολίης ἐπελήθετο τέχνης 4.455 {{Refs|cf. Hes. “Th.” 560}}; οὐδ᾽ ὣς σχεδίης ἐπελήθετο 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 5.324; γονέων ἐπιλάθεται (_Doric dialect_) {{Refs 5th c.BC+|S. “El.” 146 (Lyric poetry), compare 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.4, Lys. 26.1, etc.; ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν ὀλίγου ἐμαυτοῦ ἐπελαθόμην 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Ap.” [same place]: proverbial, Μαλέας δὲ κάμψας ἐπιλάθου τῶν οἴκαδε 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 8.6.20: with _accusative_, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.46, E. “Hel.” 265, Ar. “Nu.” 631; ὑπὸ χρόνου τι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Phaedo” 73e}}: c._infinitive_, {{Refs|Ar. “V.” 853, Pl. “R.” 563b, Hyp. “Lyc.” 8: with}}_participle_, ὀφείλων ἐπιλέλᾱθα I **forgot** **that** I owed, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Pi. “O.” 10(11).3, cf. E. “Ba.” 188: with a _preposition_, ἐ. περὶ τῶν πεπραγμένων 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.148}}; περὶ οὗ.., περὶ ὅτου.., {{Refs|Pl. “Prt.” 334d, 336d}}; **leave disregarded, neglect**, πρόσταγμα 1st c.AD: Cebes Philosophus 24.
**II.2**. less frequently, **forget wilfully**, τῶν ἐντολέων μεμνημένος ἐπελανθάνετο 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.147; ἑκὼν ἐπιλήθομαι {{Refs|[prev. author] 4.43, compare 3.75, Aeschin. 1.158.}}
1953:
** ἐπιλησμ-ονή**, ἡ,
**forgetfulness**, {{LXX|Cratin. 410 cited in Scholia Ar. “Nu.” 788, LXX.Sir.11.27; ἀκροατὴς -λησμονῆς “Epistle of James” 1.25}}:—also **ἐπιλησμονείη** (sic), 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus, and **ἐπιλήσμη** {{Refs|Alex. 315.}}
1965:
** ἐπίορκ-ος**, ον,
**sworn falsely**, of oaths, εἰ δέ τι τῶνδ᾽ ἐπίορκον 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 19.264: frequently in the phrase ἐπίορκον ὀμόσσαι take **a false oath**, swear **falsely**, {{Refs|3.279, 19.260, Hes. “Op.” 282, “Th.” 232}}; in full, ἐπίορκον ὅρκον ὤμοσε {{Refs|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 150; and so ἐ. ἐπομνύναι (see. ἐπόμνυμι); but in Il. 10.332 ἐ. ἐπώμοσε}} he swore **a bootless oath**, i.e. one which he meant to fulfil, but the gods willed otherwise.
**II**. of persons, **forsworn, perjured**, {{Refs|Hes. “Op.” 804, “Schwyzer” 179a (from Crete), E. “El.” 1355 (_anapaest meter_), Ar. “Nu.” 399, +others}}: _superlative_ **-ότατος** 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 6.48. _adverb_ **-κως** 2nd c.AD: Herodianus Grammaticus 6.9.2.
1967:
** ἐπιούσιος**, ον,
either, **sufficient for the coming** (and so _current_) **day**, (ἐπιοῦσα (i.e. ἡμέρα)), or, **for the day** (ἐπὶ τὴν οὖσαν (i.e. ἡμέραν)), ἄρτος NT.Matthew.6.11 {{NT|“NT.Luke.11.3”}}; τὰ ἐ. uncertain meaning {{Refs|compare (“Phil.Woch.” 47.889) in “Sammelb.” 5224.20. (Very rare word in Origen's day, “De Orat.” 27.7.)}}
1971:
** ἐπιποθ-έω**,
**desire besides** or **yearn after**, c._accusative_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 5.93, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.598}}; **feel the want of**, {{LXX+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 855e; ἐ. τινός LXX.Psa.118(119).20; ἐπί τι [prev. work] 61 (62). 11.}}
1972:
** ἐπιπόθ-ησις**, εως, ἡ,
**longing after**, τινός {{NT+2nd c.AD+|NT.2Cor.7.7, 2nd c.AD: Aquila LXX.Eze.23.11, 5th-6th c.AD: Damascius Philosophus “de Principiis” 38.}}
1973:
** ἐπιπόθ-ητος**, ον,
**longed for, desired,** {{NT|NT.Phil.4.1}}; **missed, found** **wanting**, ὅρκοι {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Appianus Historicus “Ἰβηρική” 43.}}
1981:
** ἐπισκην-όω**,
**to be quartered in**, ταῖς οἰκίαις {{Refs 2nd c.BC+|2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.72.1; ἐπὶ τὰς οἰκίας [prev. work] 18.8}}: _metaphorically_, **dwell upon**, ἡ δύναμις ἐ. ἐπί τινα {{NT|NT.2Cor.12.9.}}
1991:
** ἐπιστηρ-ίζω**,
**cause** **to rest on**, ἐπιστηριῶ ἐπί σε τοὺς ὀφθαλμούς μου{{LXX|LXX.Psa.31(32).8}}; **make** **to lean on**, τί τινι {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Oppianus Apamensis Epicus “Cynegetica” 4.256}}; **set over**, Δεῖμον κεραυνῷ {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th-5th c.AD(?): Nonnus Epicus “Dionysiaca” 2.417}}; **confirm**, τινά {{NT|NT.Act.15.32}}:—_passive_, **to be supported**, ἐν τῷ ὕδατι {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Problemata” 933a10; τινί 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Ind.” 6}}; ἐπιστηριχθήσομαι and ἐπεστηρίχθη ἐπὶ [τοὺς κίονας], {{LXX+2nd c.AD+|LXX.Judg.16.26, 29, compare 2nd c.AD: Aquila LXX.Exo.17.12.}}
